statements.statement:
Let \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and define \(\widetilde S^0\), \(\widetilde s\), \(\widetilde Y_m\), and \(\widetilde\Gamma\) as in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Put \(Y_m=(S^0_{0,m}-s_0,S^0_{1,m}-s_1)\) and \(\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}Y_m\otimes Y_m\). There is a constant \(C_*<\infty\), depending only on the fixed model constants and \(r\), such that
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g)\quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}),
 \qquad
 \max_{p,m}\|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
When \(d>0\), for every sufficiently fine grid the operator \(\widetilde\Gamma\) has exactly \(d\) positive eigenvalues, its \(d\)-th eigenvalue is at least \(\gamma_-^2/2\), and its selected projector \(\widetilde\Pi\) satisfies
\[
 \|\widetilde\Pi-\Pi\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
If \(\widetilde b_p\) denotes any selected positive-square-root factor coordinates of \(\widetilde\Gamma\), there is an orthogonal matrix \(R_{\mathcal G}\) such that
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\|\widetilde b_p-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}b_p\|_{L^2}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
Consequently, with \(H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0b_0^\top\) and \(\widetilde H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widetilde b_0\widetilde b_0^\top\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H_0)\ge\kappa_-/2,
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde H_0^{-1}-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0^{-1}R_{\mathcal G}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
The population comparison curve is exact for the interpolated panel:
\[
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta
 \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal I,
 \qquad
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}(g)=\theta(g)
 \quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D});
\]
and for \(d=0\), the factor, projector, and Gram assertions use the zero-dimensional convention and the last display holds with \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_1\).
statements.justification: This lemma closes the internal interpolation gap by stabilizing the population factor map before differentiation.
statements.gap: The existing grid proposition controls only output interpolation; it does not control the covariance operator and pre-period inverse computed from interpolated curves.
statements.consumer: The gridwise functional-PCR expansion is centered at this stable interpolated population map.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), write
\(h=h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and put
\(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\).  The hazard identity and endpoint
normalization give
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)
 =\exp\left\{-\int_0^t\lambda^0_{p,m}(u)\,du\right\}.        \tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:hazard\mbox{-}smoothness}\), the product rule applied to
\((S^0_{p,m})'=-\lambda^0_{p,m}S^0_{p,m}\) gives a uniform
\(C^{\beta+1}\) bound on every cell survival curve.  The piecewise-linear
interpolation remainder on each grid interval is therefore bounded by
\(C_*h^{q_\beta}\).  Interpolation reproduces its input at every knot, so
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g),
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le C_*h^{q_\beta}.                                        \tag{2}
\]
Because averaging and centering are linear and every cell uses the same
grid,
\[
 \widetilde s_p=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_p,
 \qquad
 \widetilde Y_m=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}Y_m.                 \tag{3}
\]
The donor incoherence and factor envelope assumptions give
\(\sup_m\|Y_m\|_{L^2}\le C\).  Equations (2)--(3), the fixed horizon, and
the triangle inequality give
\[
 \sup_m\|\widetilde Y_m-Y_m\|_{L^2}\le Ch^{q_\beta}.         \tag{4}
\]
For rank-one operators,
\(\|x\otimes y\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=\|x\|_2\|y\|_2\).  Hence
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\\
 &\le N_0^{-1}\sum_m
 \{\|\widetilde Y_m-Y_m\|_2\|Y_m\|_2
   +\|\widetilde Y_m\|_2\|\widetilde Y_m-Y_m\|_2\}\\
 &\le C_*h^{q_\beta}.                                      \tag{5}
 \end{split}
\]

Assume \(d>0\).  The canonical donor normalization gives
\[
 \Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_mY_m\otimes Y_m
       =\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k^2u_k\otimes u_k.               \tag{6}
\]
Thus \(\lambda_d(\Gamma)\ge\gamma_-^2\) and
\(\lambda_{d+1}(\Gamma)=0\).  Also (3) and the normalized factor model show
that \(\widetilde Y_m=(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}b)^\top z_m\), so
\(\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde\Gamma)\le d\).  The variational
characterization of ordered eigenvalues and (5) imply
\[
 |\lambda_k(\widetilde\Gamma)-\lambda_k(\Gamma)|
 \le\|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}.              \tag{7}
\]
For all sufficiently fine grids, (5)--(7) give
\(\lambda_d(\widetilde\Gamma)\ge\gamma_-^2/2\); together with the rank
bound, this proves that \(\widetilde\Gamma\) has exactly \(d\) positive
eigenvalues.

Let \(\mathscr C\) be a fixed contour separating
\([\gamma_-^2/2,2\gamma_+^2]\) from a neighborhood of zero.  Finite-rank
spectral calculus and the resolvent identity give
\[
 \widetilde\Pi-\Pi
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\mathscr C}
 (z-\widetilde\Gamma)^{-1}(\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma)
 (z-\Gamma)^{-1}\,dz.                                      \tag{8}
\]
The two resolvents on \(\mathscr C\) are bounded only by the fixed spectral
gap.  Equations (5) and (8) yield
\[
 \|\widetilde\Pi-\Pi\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ch^{q_\beta}.        \tag{9}
\]
Applying the same contour identity with the analytic function \(z^{1/2}\)
on the positive spectral component shows that the selected positive square
roots differ by at most \(Ch^{q_\beta}\) in operator norm.  Choose
orthonormal coordinate frames for the two selected ranges and align them
by the polar factor of their cross-Gram matrix.  Equation (9) makes that
cross-Gram matrix invertible, and the polar identity supplies an orthogonal
matrix \(R_{\mathcal G}\) for which
\[
 \max_p\|\widetilde b_p-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}b_p\|_{L^2}
 \le Ch^{q_\beta}.                                         \tag{10}
\]
This formulation is insensitive to internal eigenvalue ties.

By the pre-contrast Gram assumption,
\(\lambda_{\min}(H_0)\ge\kappa_-\).  From (10), the factor envelope, and
\(xx^\top-yy^\top=(x-y)x^\top+y(x-y)^\top\),
\[
 \|\widetilde H_0-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0R_{\mathcal G}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le Ch^{q_\beta}.                                         \tag{11}
\]
For a sufficiently fine grid the right side is at most \(\kappa_-/2\),
so \(\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H_0)\ge\kappa_-/2\).  Finally,
\[
 A^{-1}-B^{-1}=A^{-1}(B-A)B^{-1}                           \tag{12}
\]
with \(A=\widetilde H_0\) and
\(B=R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0R_{\mathcal G}\) proves the asserted inverse
bound.

It remains to identify the comparison curve.  Linearity of
\(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) and the normalized factor model give, for the
same target loading,
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,\star}-\widetilde s_p
 =\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(b_p^\top z_\star).                \tag{13}
\]
The interpolated pre-factor Gram is nonsingular by (11), so the population
least-squares step recovers the coordinates of \(z_\star\) in the rotated
interpolated factor basis exactly.  Substitution in the post-period factor
map yields
\[
 \begin{split}
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}
 &=\widetilde s_1+\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(b_1^\top z_\star)\\
 &=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(s_1+b_1^\top z_\star)
 =\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta.                            \tag{14}
 \end{split}
\]
Equation (2) at the knots proves the asserted grid equality.  When \(d=0\),
every factor calculation is an empty sum, and (14) reduces to
\(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_1\).
\(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and let \((\bar b_p,\bar z_m)\) be any donor-centered compatible \(d\)-coordinate representation of the normalized factor model. After covariance normalization of its donor loadings, the donor-SVD factors and loadings in \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}factorization}\) equal the compatible factors and loadings up to a common orthogonal transform. If \(d>0\), then \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0\) belongs to the span of the canonical \(b_0\), the matrix \(H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0b_0^\top\) is positive definite, and
\[
 z_\star=H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)
 \{S^0_{0,\star}(t)-s_0(t)\}\,dt
\]
is the unique compatible target coordinate. For \(d=0\), compatibility forces \(S^0_{p,m}=s_p\) for all units.
statements.justification: This supplies the missing algebra from target-pre factor compatibility to the unique canonical target loading.
statements.gap: A donor-operator SVD alone does not establish target span inclusion; the lemma uses the model's compatible all-unit factorization and the positive pre-period Gram.
statements.consumer: It validates the causal target coordinate used by functional PCR and the Han--Shah structural embedding.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), suppress the sample-size indices,
and put \(\mathcal H=L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\).  Let
\((\bar b_p,\bar z_m)\) be the compatible representation in the statement.
Thus
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)-s_p(t)=\bar b_p(t)^\top\bar z_m,
 \qquad m\in\mathcal M.                                  \tag{1}
\]
Because \(s_p\) is the donor mean in
\(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}factorization}\), averaging (1) over
\(m\in\mathcal D\) and using donor centering gives the same centered donor
curves in every compatible representation.

Define \(\bar B:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal H\) and
\(\bar Z\in\mathbb R^{N_0\times d}\) by
\[
 (\bar Bx)_p(t)=\bar b_p(t)^\top x,
 \qquad \bar Z_{m\cdot}=\bar z_m^\top.                  \tag{2}
\]
For every \(a\in\mathbf 1^\perp\), the definition of the centered donor
operator and (1) give
\[
 \mathcal C_Da
 =\bar B\left(N_0^{-1/2}\bar Z^\top a\right).           \tag{3}
\]
By exact centered rank, \(\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal C_D)=d\).  Since
(3) factors \(\mathcal C_D\) through \(\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 d=\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal C_D)
 \leq\min\{\operatorname{rank}(\bar B),
             \operatorname{rank}(\bar Z)\}\leq d.       \tag{4}
\]
Thus \(\bar B\) and \(\bar Z\) both have rank \(d\).  This conclusion uses
only compatibility and exact centered rank, not the pre-period Gram condition.

The donor loading covariance
\[
 \Sigma=N_0^{-1}\bar Z^\top\bar Z                       \tag{5}
\]
is therefore positive definite.  Covariance-normalize by setting
\[
 \widetilde b_p=\Sigma^{1/2}\bar b_p,
 \qquad \widetilde z_m=\Sigma^{-1/2}\bar z_m.           \tag{6}
\]
Then
\[
 \widetilde b_p(t)^\top\widetilde z_m
 =\bar b_p(t)^\top\bar z_m,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \widetilde z_m\widetilde z_m^\top=I_d.                 \tag{7}
\]
Let \(\widetilde Bx=(\widetilde b_0^\top x,
\widetilde b_1^\top x)\), and put
\(Y_m=(S^0_{0,m}-s_0,S^0_{1,m}-s_1)\in\mathcal H\).  Equation (7) yields
\[
 \Gamma:=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}Y_m\otimes Y_m
 =\widetilde B\widetilde B^*.                            \tag{8}
\]

Let \(B:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal H\) be the canonical donor-SVD factor map,
so \((Bx)_p=b_p^\top x\).  The singular-value construction gives
\[
 \mathcal C_D\mathcal C_D^*=BB^*.                        \tag{9}
\]
Donor centering also gives directly
\[
 \mathcal C_D\mathcal C_D^*
 =N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}Y_m\otimes Y_m=\Gamma.   \tag{10}
\]
Indeed, for \(f\in\mathcal H\), the vector with entries
\(N_0^{-1/2}\langle Y_m,f\rangle_{\mathcal H}\) lies in
\(\mathbf 1^\perp\), and applying \(\mathcal C_D\) to that vector gives the
middle operator in (10).  Combining (8)--(10),
\[
 BB^*=\widetilde B\widetilde B^*.                        \tag{11}
\]
Both maps have rank \(d\), so their ranges coincide.  Let
\(B^\dagger=(B^*B)^{-1}B^*\) be the left inverse of \(B\), and define
\[
 R=B^\dagger\widetilde B.                                \tag{12}
\]
Range equality gives \(BR=\widetilde B\).  Moreover, (11) implies
\[
 RR^*=B^\dagger\widetilde B\widetilde B^*B^{\dagger *}
     =B^\dagger BB^*B^{\dagger *}=I_d.                  \tag{13}
\]
Hence \(R\) is orthogonal and
\[
 b_p=R\widetilde b_p.                                    \tag{14}
\]
For a donor \(m\), injectivity of \(B\), (7), and
\(BR=\widetilde B\) give
\[
 Bz_m=Y_m=\widetilde B\widetilde z_m=BR\widetilde z_m
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad z_m=R\widetilde z_m.        \tag{15}
\]
Thus the covariance-normalized compatible factors and loadings equal the
canonical donor-SVD coordinates up to one common orthogonal transformation.
The deterministic sign and tie-breaking rule merely chooses a representative
within this orthogonal equivalence class.

Assume \(d>0\).  Compatibility for the target unit and (6), (14) give
\[
 S^0_{0,\star}-s_0
 =\widetilde b_0^\top\widetilde z_\star
 =b_0^\top R\widetilde z_\star.                          \tag{16}
\]
Thus the target-pre contrast belongs to the span of the canonical pre-period
factors.  Now, and only now, use the positive pre-contrast Gram assumption:
\[
 H_0:=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt,
 \qquad \lambda_{\min}(H_0)\geq\kappa_->0.              \tag{17}
\]
Therefore \(H_0\) is invertible.  Multiplying (16) by \(b_0(t)\),
integrating, and applying (17) yields
\[
 R\widetilde z_\star
 =H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)
 \{S^0_{0,\star}(t)-s_0(t)\}\,dt.                       \tag{18}
\]
If \(x\) and \(x'\) are two compatible canonical target coefficients, then
\(b_0^\top(x-x')=0\) in \(L^2(\mathcal I)\), whence
\[
 0=\int_{\mathcal I}\{b_0(t)^\top(x-x')\}^2\,dt
  =(x-x')^\top H_0(x-x').                                \tag{19}
\]
Positive definiteness forces \(x=x'\).  Hence (18) is the unique compatible
target coordinate and is exactly the \(z_\star\) selected in the canonical
construction.

If \(d=0\), a compatible \(d\)-coordinate representation has an empty factor
term, so (1) reads \(S^0_{p,m}=s_p\) for every period and every unit.  This
proves the zero-dimensional assertion and completes the proof. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix an observed control cell or deterministic half-fold containing \(k\) patients, put \(h_0=s_-g_-\), \(\ell_k=\max\{1,kh_0/8\}\), and let \(\widehat S_k^\dagger\) be the stabilized product-limit curve in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). For all sufficiently large \(k\): (i) \(\widehat S_k^\dagger\) equals the ordinary Kaplan--Meier curve on \(\{Y_k(\bar\tau)\ge\ell_k\}\); (ii)
\[
 P\{Y_k(\bar\tau)<kh_0/8\}
 \le \exp\{-49h_0k/128\}\le e^{-c_0k},
 \qquad c_0=h_0/3;
\]
(iii) changing one patient record changes the entire interpolated stabilized curve by at most \(C/k\), deterministically on every dataset; (iv) every individual observed multiplier contribution has supremum norm at most \(C/k\), deterministically; and (v), with \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\), there are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes \(\varphi_{k,j}\), a deterministic bias \(b_k^\dagger\), and a centered remainder \(q_k^\dagger\) such that
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger-\widetilde S^0
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_{k,j}+b_k^\dagger+q_k^\dagger,
 \qquad
 \|b_k^\dagger\|_\infty\le Ce^{-c_0k},
 \qquad
 E\|q_k^\dagger\|_\infty^2\le Ck^{-2}.
\]
For independent donor cells, their centered rare-cell contributions average with second moment at most \(CN_0^{-1}e^{-c_0k}\le C(N_0k^2)^{-1}\). All assertions allow ties and all realized risk sets; no all-cells-good event is imposed.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Suppress the cell label.  For patient \(j\), define
\[
 N_j(u)=\mathbf 1\{X_j\leq u,\Delta_j=1\},\qquad
 Y_j(u)=\mathbf 1\{X_j\geq u\},\qquad
 M_j(u)=N_j(u)-\int_0^uY_j(v)\lambda^0(v)\,dv.             \tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:control\mbox{-}consistency}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}censoring}\), the last integral is the
compensator of \(N_j\).  By
\(\mathrm{ass:patient\mbox{-}independence}\), the processes \(M_j\) are
independent, mean-zero, square-integrable martingales.  Put
\[
 Y=\sum_{j=1}^kY_j,\qquad N=\sum_{j=1}^kN_j,
 \qquad M=\sum_{j=1}^kM_j,
 \qquad H(u)=E Y_j(u)=S^0(u)G(u).
\]
The event- and censor-overlap assumptions give the uniform risk lower bound
\[
 H(u)\geq h_0:=s_-g_->0,
 \qquad u\in\mathcal I.                                  \tag{2}
\]

We first treat ties and clipping.  At a tied failure time, order failures by
patient index and remove each earlier ordered failure from the risk set before
processing the next.  If the pre-tie risk set is \(y\) and there are \(a\)
failures, then
\[
 \prod_{q=0}^{a-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{y-q}\right)=1-\frac{a}{y}. \tag{3}
\]
Thus this measurable ordered convention agrees with the ordinary
product-limit factor.  On the ordered event axis set
\[
 Y^\dagger(u)=\max\{Y(u),\ell_k\},
 \qquad \ell_k=\max\{1,kh_0/8\}.
\]
Every stabilized product factor lies in \([0,1]\).  If
\(Y(\bar\tau)\geq\ell_k\), monotonicity of the risk process gives
\(Y(u)\geq\ell_k\) at every earlier event.  No denominator is then clipped,
and (3) proves assertion (i).

The variables \(Y_j(\bar\tau)\) are independent Bernoulli variables and
\(\mu:=E Y(\bar\tau)\geq kh_0\).  For \(s>0\), independence gives
\[
 E e^{-sY(\bar\tau)}
 \leq \exp\{(e^{-s}-1)\mu\}.
\]
Exponential Markov inequality, optimized at
\(s=-\log(1-\delta)\), together with
\((1-\delta)\log(1-\delta)+\delta\geq\delta^2/2\), yields
\[
 P\{Y(\bar\tau)\leq(1-\delta)\mu\}
 \leq e^{-\delta^2\mu/2},
 \qquad 0<\delta<1.                                      \tag{4}
\]
Because \(kh_0/8\leq\mu/8\), taking \(\delta=7/8\) proves
\[
 P\{Y(\bar\tau)<kh_0/8\}
 \leq e^{-49h_0k/128}
 \leq e^{-h_0k/3}=e^{-c_0k},
 \qquad c_0=h_0/3.                                       \tag{5}
\]

We next prove the deterministic guards.  For
\(f(y)=1-1/\max\{y,\ell_k\}\),
\[
 |f(y+e)-f(y)|\leq |e|\ell_k^{-2},
 \qquad |e|\leq1.                                       \tag{6}
\]
Changing one patient record inserts or deletes at most two ordered failure
factors and changes each remaining ordered risk count by at most one.  The
telescoping identity for products of numbers in \([0,1]\), (6), and the fact
that there are at most \(k\) failure factors give, for all sufficiently large
\(k\),
\[
 \sup_{t\in\mathcal I}
 |\widehat S_k^\dagger(t;O)-\widehat S_k^\dagger(t;O')|
 \leq 2\ell_k^{-1}+k\ell_k^{-2}\leq C/k.                \tag{7}
\]
Piecewise-linear interpolation is a contraction in supremum norm.  A patient
has at most one observed failure, so its observed product-limit multiplier
contribution is bounded, on every dataset, by
\[
 \sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\widehat S_k^\dagger(t-)
 \int_0^t\{Y^\dagger(u)\}^{-1}\,dN_j(u)
 \leq\ell_k^{-1}\leq C/k.                               \tag{8}
\]
This proves assertions (iii) and (iv), including exhausted-risk datasets.

For the stochastic expansion, put \(R=\widehat S_k^\dagger/S^0\) on the
ordered event-time axis.  The product-integral equations, (1), and integration
by parts give the exact clipped ratio identity
\[
 R(t)-1
 =-\int_0^tR(u-)\{Y^\dagger(u)\}^{-1}\,dM(u)
  +\int_0^tR(u-)\left\{1-\frac{Y(u)}{Y^\dagger(u)}\right\}
             \lambda^0(u)\,du.                           \tag{9}
\]
This is an identity on every dataset, not an approximation on a good-risk-set
event.  Since every stabilized product factor lies in \([0,1]\), event overlap
implies \(0\leq R\leq s_-^{-1}\).  The drift in (9) is supported on
\(\{Y(u)<\ell_k\}\), which by monotonicity is contained in
\(\{Y(\bar\tau)<\ell_k\}\).  Hazard smoothness gives
\(\int_0^{\bar\tau}\lambda^0(u)\,du\leq L\bar\tau\).
If \(A_k\) denotes the drift in (9) after multiplication by \(S^0(t)\),
then (5) yields
\[
 \|EA_k\|_\infty\leq Ce^{-c_0k},
 \qquad
 E\|A_k-EA_k\|_\infty^2\leq Ce^{-c_0k}.                \tag{10}
\]

Define the independent mean-zero influence processes
\[
 \varphi_{k,j}^{\circ}(t)
 =-S^0(t)\int_0^tH(u)^{-1}\,dM_j(u).                    \tag{11}
\]
After subtracting \(k^{-1}\sum_j\varphi_{k,j}^{\circ}\) from (9), the
remaining martingale component is
\[
 V_k(t)=-S^0(t)\int_0^tD_k(u)\,dM(u),
 \qquad
 D_k(u)=\frac{R(u-)}{Y^\dagger(u)}-\frac{1}{kH(u)}.      \tag{12}
\]
Let \(\mathcal E_k=\{Y(\bar\tau)\geq kh_0/2\}\).  On
\(\mathcal E_k\), one has \(Y^\dagger=Y\), and the exact algebraic
decomposition
\[
 D_k
 =\frac{R-1}{Y}-\frac{Y-kH}{kHY}                       \tag{13}
\]
holds.  Stop (9) immediately before \(Y<kh_0/2\).  The predictable
isometry, Doob's \(L^2\) inequality, (2), and patient independence give
\[
 E\{\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_k}\|R-1\|_\infty^2\}
 \leq Ck^{-1},
 \qquad
 E\{Y(u)-kH(u)\}^2\leq k.                               \tag{14}
\]
Substituting (13)--(14) into the predictable quadratic variation yields
\[
 E\left[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_k}
 \int_0^{\bar\tau}D_k(u)^2Y(u)\lambda^0(u)\,du\right]
 \leq Ck^{-2}.                                           \tag{15}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_k^c\), clipping and (2) give
\(|D_k|\leq C/k\).  The fourth-moment martingale inequality followed by
Cauchy--Schwarz and the Chernoff calculation in (4) gives
\[
 E\left[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_k^c}
 \int_0^{\bar\tau}D_k(u)^2Y(u)\lambda^0(u)\,du\right]
 \leq Ck^{-1}e^{-ck/2}\leq Ck^{-2}.                     \tag{16}
\]
Doob's inequality applied to (12) now proves
\(E\|V_k\|_\infty^2\leq Ck^{-2}\).  Set
\[
 b_k^\dagger=EA_k,
 \qquad q_k^{\dagger,\circ}=V_k+A_k-EA_k.               \tag{17}
\]
Equations (10), (15)--(17) prove the bias and centered-remainder bounds on
the event-time axis.  Apply the deterministic operator
\(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) to (11) and (17), and denote the resulting
processes by \(\varphi_{k,j}\) and \(q_k^\dagger\).  Interpolation preserves
means and supremum bounds and changes the deterministic center to
\(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\).  This proves assertion (v).

It remains to prove the donor rare-cell assertion without a grid union.  We
first record and prove the required ordered bounded-variation inequality.  If
\(F_1,\ldots,F_N\) are independent random c\`adl\`ag functions with
\(F_m(0)=0\), then
\[
 E\left\|N^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^N(F_m-EF_m)\right\|_\infty^2
 \leq \frac{16}{N^2}\sum_{m=1}^N
 E\{\operatorname{TV}(F_m)^2\}.                          \tag{18}
\]
To verify (18), condition first on deterministic bounded-variation paths and
write their Jordan decompositions.  A positive variation component is
\(F_m^+(t)=\mu_m^+([0,t])\), where \(\mu_m^+\) is a positive measure of
mass \(a_m^+\).  Introduce an auxiliary time \(T_m^+\) with conditional law
\(\mu_m^+/a_m^+\).  Conditional Jensen inequality gives
\[
 E_\epsilon\sup_t\left|\sum_m\epsilon_mF_m^+(t)\right|^2
 \leq E_{\epsilon,T}\sup_t
 \left|\sum_m\epsilon_ma_m^+\mathbf 1\{T_m^+\leq t\}\right|^2. \tag{19}
\]
Given the auxiliary times, ordering donors by \(T_m^+\) turns the process on
the right into partial sums of independent mean-zero variables
\(\epsilon_ma_m^+\).  Doob's scalar \(L^2\) inequality bounds (19) by
\(4\sum_m(a_m^+)^2\).  The same argument applies to the negative variation
components.  Conditional symmetrization with an independent copy and
\(a_m^++a_m^-\leq\operatorname{TV}(F_m)\) proves (18), after enlarging the
universal constant.  Step-function approximation in variation norm and Fatou's
lemma remove continuity and atom restrictions.  This argument is ordered in
time and uses a donor-index martingale; it does not involve the number of grid
points.

For donor cell \(m\), let \(A_{k,m}\) be the rare drift from (10).  The
cumulative integral in (9) is increasing, \(S_m^0\) has total variation at
most one, and the cumulative integral is uniformly bounded.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(A_{k,m})
 \leq C\mathbf 1\{Y_m(\bar\tau)<\ell_k\}.                \tag{20}
\]
With \(U_m=A_{k,m}-EA_{k,m}\), one has
\(EU_m(t)=0\) for every \(t\), and Jensen's inequality, (20), and (5) give
\[
 E\{\operatorname{TV}(U_m)^2\}\leq Ce^{-c_0k}.
\]
Apply (18) to the independent centered processes \(U_m\).  For all
sufficiently large \(k\),
\[
 E\left\|N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}U_m\right\|_\infty^2
 \leq CN_0^{-1}e^{-c_0k}
 \leq C(N_0k^2)^{-1}.                                    \tag{21}
\]
This proves the last assertion without an all-cells-good event and completes
the proof. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose \(r=1\), put \(n_D=N_0K_D\),
\[
 \bar G_D(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}G_{1,m}(t),
 \qquad H_D(t)=s_1(t)\bar G_D(t).
\]
For the continuously interpolated pooled donor-post product-limit estimator in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\), there are independent mean-zero processes
\[
 \phi_{m,j}^{\mathrm{pool}}(t)
 =-s_1(t)\int_0^tH_D(u)^{-1}\,dM_{m,j}(u)
\]
such that, on the inference grid,
\[
 \widehat\theta_1-\theta
 =n_D^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j=1}^{K_D}
 \mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\phi_{m,j}^{\mathrm{pool}}
 +b_{D,n_D}+q_{D,n_D},
\]
where
\[
 \|b_{D,n_D}\|_\infty\le Ce^{-cn_D},
 \qquad Eq_{D,n_D}=0,
 \qquad E\|q_{D,n_D}\|_\infty^2\le Cn_D^{-2},
\]
uniformly over the rank-one class although the censoring laws may differ across donors. If \(\widehat Z_1^\xi\) is the explicit pooled multiplier and \(\Sigma_1\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_1\) are respectively the covariance kernel of the first-order sum and the conditional covariance kernel of that multiplier, then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_1}E_P
 \left\|n_D^{-1}\sum_{m,j}
 \mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\phi_{m,j}^{\mathrm{pool}}\right\|_
 {\infty,\mathcal I}^2
 +\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_1}E_PE_\xi
 \|\widehat Z_1^\xi\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}^2
 \le Cn_D^{-1},
\]
and
\[
 n_D\|\widehat\Sigma_1-\Sigma_1\|_{\infty,\mathcal I^2}
 \longrightarrow0
\]
in probability uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_1\). These assertions allow variance-zero coordinates, including time zero. No random-quantile coverage assertion is made.
statements.justification: This is the missing pooled rank-one product-limit and patient-multiplier theorem under donor-specific censoring.
statements.gap: A one-cell Kaplan--Meier expansion does not justify pooling independent but non-identically censored donor cohorts.
statements.consumer: It closes the exact-rank-one attaining rate and supplies the implementation-level pooled multiplier.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(n=n_D=N_0K_D\) and index donor-post patients by \(i=(m,j)\). By normalization collapse, all donor-post failure times have survival \(s_1\) and common hazard \(\lambda_1\), although \(G_{1,m}\) may vary. Define
\[
 N_i(u)=\mathbf1\{X_i\le u,\Delta_i=1\},\quad
 Y_i(u)=\mathbf1\{X_i\ge u\},\quad
 M_i(u)=N_i(u)-\int_0^uY_i(v)\lambda_1(v)\,dv.            \tag{1}
\]
Consistency and independent censoring give the compensator, and patient independence makes the \(M_i\) independent mean-zero martingales. With \(Y=\sum_iY_i\), \(N=\sum_iN_i\), and \(M=\sum_iM_i\),
\[
 EY(u)=nH_D(u),\qquad H_D(u)=s_1(u)\bar G_D(u)\ge h_0:=s_-g_->0. \tag{2}
\]
An exponential lower-tail bound for the independent risk indicators and a time-ordering symmetrization give
\[
 P\{Y(\bar\tau)<nh_0/2\}\le e^{-cn},\qquad
 E\sup_u|Y(u)/n-H_D(u)|^2\le Cn^{-1}.                    \tag{3}
\]
For the second display, conditional Rademacher sums indexed by \(u\) are reverse partial sums after ordering the observed times, so the scalar maximal inequality applies without identical censoring laws.

Let \(\widehat S_D^{\mathrm{PL}}\) be the pooled product-limit curve, \(J_Y=\mathbf1\{Y>0\}\), and \(R=\widehat S_D^{\mathrm{PL}}/s_1\). Product integration gives the exact identity
\[
 R(t)-1=-\int_0^tR(u-)\frac{J_Y(u)}{Y(u)}\,dM(u)
 +\int_0^tR(u-)\{1-J_Y(u)\}\lambda_1(u)\,du.             \tag{4}
\]
The convention \(J_Y/Y=0\) on an empty risk set avoids every boundary division. Stopping before \(Y<nh_0/2\), predictable isometry, \(0\le R\le s_-^{-1}\), and (3) give
\[
 E\sup_{t\le\bar\tau}|R(t)-1|^2\le Cn^{-1}+Ce^{-cn}.     \tag{5}
\]

Define
\[
 \phi_i^{\mathrm{pool}}(t)=-s_1(t)\int_0^tH_D(u)^{-1}\,dM_i(u). \tag{6}
\]
These processes are independent and mean zero. Subtracting \(n^{-1}\sum_i\phi_i^{\mathrm{pool}}\) from (4) leaves the martingale integrand
\[
 D_n(u)=R(u-)\frac{J_Y(u)}{Y(u)}-\frac1{nH_D(u)}.          \tag{7}
\]
On \(\{Y(\bar\tau)\ge nh_0/2\}\),
\[
 |D_n(u)|\le \frac{C}{n}|R(u-)-1|
 +\frac{C}{n}|Y(u)/n-H_D(u)|.                             \tag{8}
\]
Equations (3), (5), (8), and predictable isometry yield an \(L^2\)-supremum bound \(Cn^{-2}\) for the resulting martingale remainder. On the complement, the ordered failure risks are distinct positive integers, so
\[
 \int J_Y/Y\,dN\le\sum_{k=1}^nk^{-1}\le1+\log n;         \tag{9}
\]
combining (9) with the exponential probability in (3) gives the same polynomial bound. The drift in (4) is uniformly bounded and vanishes unless \(Y(\bar\tau)=0\). Therefore, with its expectation denoted by \(b_{D,n}^{\mathrm{PL}}\) and the centered remainder by \(q_{D,n}^{\mathrm{PL}}\),
\[
 \widehat S_D^{\mathrm{PL}}-s_1
 =n^{-1}\sum_i\phi_i^{\mathrm{pool}}
 +b_{D,n}^{\mathrm{PL}}+q_{D,n}^{\mathrm{PL}},             \tag{10}
\]
\[
 \|b_{D,n}^{\mathrm{PL}}\|_\infty\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad
 Eq_{D,n}^{\mathrm{PL}}=0,\qquad
 E\|q_{D,n}^{\mathrm{PL}}\|_\infty^2\le Cn^{-2}.         \tag{11}
\]
Applying the deterministic interpolation contraction \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) proves the asserted grid expansion.

Predictable isometry applied to (6) gives
\[
 E\left\|n^{-1}\sum_i\phi_i^{\mathrm{pool}}\right\|_\infty^2
 \le \frac4n\int_0^{\bar\tau}\frac{\lambda_1(u)}{H_D(u)}\,du
 \le Cn^{-1}.                                             \tag{12}
\]
Conditionally on the observations, the multiplier is a Gaussian partial-sum process in failure-time order. Hence
\[
 E_\xi\|\widehat Z_1^\xi\|_\infty^2
 \le4\int_0^{\bar\tau}\frac{J_Y(u)}{Y(u)^2}\,dN(u).     \tag{13}
\]
On the event in (3) this is \(O(n^{-1})\); on its complement it is bounded by \(4\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}\). Averaging and using (3) proves the second moment assertion.

Finally, the oracle and empirical covariance kernels are
\[
 \Sigma_1(s,t)=\frac{s_1(s)s_1(t)}n
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\frac{\lambda_1(u)}{H_D(u)}\,du,
\]
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_1(s,t)=\widehat S_D^{\mathrm{PL}}(s-)
 \widehat S_D^{\mathrm{PL}}(t-)
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\frac{J_Y(u)}{Y(u)^2}\,dN(u).         \tag{14}
\]
Substitute \(dN=dM+Y\lambda_1du\). Equations (3), (5), and predictable isometry imply
\[
 \sup_v\left|\int_0^v\frac{nJ_Y}{Y^2}\,dN
 -\int_0^v\frac{\lambda_1}{H_D}\,du\right|=o_P(1),
 \qquad \|\widehat S_D^{\mathrm{PL}}-s_1\|_\infty=o_P(1), \tag{15}
\]
uniformly over the class. Multiplying (14) by \(n\) and using (15) proves
\(n\|\widehat\Sigma_1-\Sigma_1\|_\infty\to0\) uniformly in probability. Bilinear interpolation is a covariance-kernel contraction. At time zero all integrals vanish, and no coordinate variance was inverted. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix \(r\ge2\), put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), and use the stabilized full-cell and odd--even half-fold inputs in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), the aggregate functional-PCR estimator has the gridwise expansion
\[
 \widehat\theta_r-\theta
 =K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
 +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j}
 +\mathfrak b_r+Q_r,
\]
where the patient processes are independent and mean zero,
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le\eta_D(K_D),
 \qquad E\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2\le C\upsilon_r^2,
\]
with \(\upsilon_r\) as in the corrected definition of \(\omega_r\). The aggregate spectral/pre-Gram threshold failure probability is at most \(Ce^{-cn_D}\), without a union over donor cells. On the regular branch, composition of the first two Fr\'echet derivatives of the coordinate-free prediction map with the stabilized inputs gives deterministic patient envelopes \(C/K_T\) for target-pre patients and \(C/(N_0K_D)\) for donor patients on every dataset. On fallback, the ordinary pooled derivative is used. Consequently, for the oracle linear process \(Z_r\) and the empirical multiplier process \(\widehat Z_r^\xi\),
\[
 \sup_PE_P\|Z_r\|_\infty^2
 +\sup_PE_PE_\xi\|\widehat Z_r^\xi\|_\infty^2
 \le C\{K_T^{-1}+n_D^{-1}\}=C\rho_r^2.
\]
All bounds are continuous-time bounds and incur no \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G|}\) factor.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), \(k_1=\lfloor K_D/2\rfloor\), and \(k_2=K_D-k_1\). Apply the stabilized product-limit lemma to the target-pre cell, all donor full cells, and both deterministic donor half-folds. Each input of size \(k\) has
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger=\widetilde S^0+k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_{k,j}
 +b_k^\dagger+q_k^\dagger,                               \tag{1}
\]
where the patient terms are independent and mean zero,
\[
 \|b_k^\dagger\|_\infty\le Ce^{-c_0k},\qquad
 E\|q_k^\dagger\|_\infty^2\le Ck^{-2},                  \tag{2}
\]
and replacing one patient changes the interpolated curve by at most \(C/k\).

For completeness, donor averaging improves the centered remainder. Write its martingale part as
\[
 V_{k,m}(t)=-S_m^0(t)\int_0^tD_{k,m}(u)\,dM_m(u),\qquad
 E\int D_{k,m}^2Y_m\lambda_m^0\le Ck^{-2}.               \tag{3}
\]
Integration by parts separates a martingale and a bounded-variation integral. Independence across donor cells, predictable isometry, and the time-ordered bounded-variation maximal inequality give
\[
 E\left\|N_0^{-1}\sum_mq_{k,m}^\dagger\right\|_\infty^2
 \le C(N_0k^2)^{-1}+CN_0^{-1}e^{-c_0k}.                  \tag{4}
\]
This calculation is in continuous time and contains no grid union.

Let \(\Gamma_{\mathcal G}\) be the interpolated population covariance operator. Independence of the odd and even folds removes the same-fold errors-in-variables term, and (1)--(2) imply
\[
 \|E\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma_{\mathcal G}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
 \le Ce^{-c_0k_1}.                                       \tag{5}
\]
One patient replacement changes \(\widehat\Gamma\) by at most \(C/(N_0K_D)\). Hilbert-space Efron--Stein and scalar bounded differences therefore give
\[
 E\|\widehat\Gamma-E\widehat\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\le Cn_D^{-1},
\]
\[
 P\{\|\widehat\Gamma-E\widehat\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
 >Cn_D^{-1/2}+x\}\le2e^{-cn_Dx^2}.                       \tag{6}
\]
The interpolated-population stability lemma supplies a fixed selected spectral gap and a pre-Gram eigenvalue at least \(\kappa_-/2\). The eigenvalue variational inequality, the spectral-projector resolvent identity, continuity of the selected positive square root, and the inverse identity therefore turn (5)--(6) into
\[
 \sup_PP(\mathcal R^c)\le Ce^{-cn_D},                    \tag{7}
\]
where \(\mathcal R\) is the aggregate regular event in the band definition. No all-cells-good event was used.

On the fixed-gap neighborhood, write the coordinate-free map as
\[
 F(s,A,x)=s_1+A_1z,\qquad
 H=A_0^*A_0,\qquad z=H^{-1}A_0^*x.                        \tag{8}
\]
Along a differentiable path,
\[
 \dot H=\dot A_0^*A_0+A_0^*\dot A_0,\qquad
 \dot z=H^{-1}\{\dot A_0^*x+A_0^*\dot x-\dot Hz\},
\]
\[
 \dot F=\dot s_1+\dot A_1z+A_1\dot z.                    \tag{9}
\]
The contour formula for the selected projector and the Sylvester equation
\[
 A\,DA[E]+DA[E]A=D(\Pi\Gamma\Pi)[E]                       \tag{10}
\]
show that the first two Fr\'echet derivatives of \(F\) are uniformly bounded; the spectral and pre-Gram lower bounds are exactly the denominators used here. Composing (9)--(10) with the all-dataset cell sensitivity gives
\[
 \|D_j^TF\|_\infty\le C/K_T,\qquad
 \|D_{p,m,j}^DF\|_\infty\le C/(N_0K_D)                 \tag{11}
\]
on every regular dataset. On fallback, the total measurable pooled derivative is used.

Taylor's formula at the interpolated population panel, (1), (4), and (7)--(11) now yield at every grid knot
\[
 \widehat\theta_r-\theta
 =K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
 +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j}
 +\mathfrak b_r+Q_r.                                      \tag{12}
\]
The population center equals \(\theta\) on the grid by canonical target-coordinate uniqueness and interpolated-population stability. The deterministic donor half-fold bias is mapped by a uniformly Lipschitz derivative, so the definition of \(C_\eta\) gives
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le\eta_D(K_D). \tag{13}
\]
The target cell remainder, averaged donor remainder, quadratic Taylor term, bias--noise interaction, and fallback terms have respective \(L^2\)-supremum orders
\[
 K_T^{-1},\quad N_0^{-1/2}K_D^{-1},\quad
 K_T^{-1}+n_D^{-1},\quad \rho_r\eta_D(K_D),\quad
 e^{-c_\dagger K_T/2}+e^{-c_\dagger n_D/2}.               \tag{14}
\]
These are precisely dominated by the registered \(\upsilon_r\). Squaring after the triangle inequality proves
\[
 E\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2\le C\upsilon_r^2.       \tag{15}
\]

Finally, each first-order term is a fixed-rank sum of a bounded-variation coefficient times a patient martingale and a time-ordered stochastic integral. Predictable isometry, the maximal inequality, (11), and independence give
\[
 E\|Z_r\|_\infty^2\le C(K_T^{-1}+n_D^{-1}).              \tag{16}
\]
Conditionally on the data, Gaussian isometry and the same ordered argument give the multiplier analogue on \(\mathcal R\); the pooled fallback contribution is absorbed using (7). Thus
\[
 E E_\xi\|\widehat Z_r^\xi\|_\infty^2
 \le C(K_T^{-1}+n_D^{-1})=C\rho_r^2.                     \tag{17}
\]
All estimates precede restriction to the grid, so no \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G|}\) factor appears. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix \(r\ge1\), and let \(n_{\mathrm{eff},r}\), \(\delta_{r,n}(\alpha)\), \(\chi_{r,n}\), and \(\tau_{r,n}\) be the deterministic sequences in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Let \(Z_r\) be the oracle patient linear process in \(\mathrm{lem:pooled\mbox{-}noniid\mbox{-}km\mbox{-}linearization}\) when \(r=1\) and in \(\mathrm{lem:stabilized\mbox{-}gridwise\mbox{-}fpcr\mbox{-}transfer}\) when \(r\ge2\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and every three-dimensional tail,
\[
 \chi_{r,n}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\tau_{r,n}}{\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}=\chi_{r,n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every sufficiently large evaluated triple,
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}
 P\left\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le \widetilde c_r^\xi+\tau_{r,n}\right\}
 \ge 1-\alpha+\frac12\delta_{r,n}(\alpha)
 \ge1-\alpha-o(1),
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_P\widetilde c_r^\xi
 \le C\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
The result permits singular covariance matrices and zero-variance coordinates, including the coordinate at time zero; \(\widetilde c_r^\xi\) is the measurable left-continuous generalized-inverse conditional \(1-\alpha+\delta_{r,n}(\alpha)\) quantile.
statements.justification: This theorem validates the data-dependent functional-PCR multiplier quantile uniformly over the canonical grid without a coordinate-variance floor.
statements.gap: Classical multiplier results do not directly cover the estimated projector, square root, inverse pre-Gram, stabilized product-limit derivatives, fallback branches, and singular coordinates in one unrestricted-relative-growth theorem.
statements.consumer: It supplies the stochastic critical radius used by the honest continuous-time functional-PCR band.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), \(m=n_{\mathrm{eff},r}\),
\(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), and
\(p_{\mathcal G}=2|\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}|\).  Abbreviate
\(\delta_{r,n}\), \(\chi_{r,n}\), and \(\tau_{r,n}\) by
\(\delta_n\), \(\chi_n\), and \(\tau_n\).  The quantities
\(a_{r,n}\), \(k_{r,n}\), \(p_{\mathrm c,r,n}\), \(U_{r,n}\), and
\(\zeta_{r,n}\) are the explicit deterministic sequences in the corrected
band construction.

\emph{Covariance and modulus derivation.}
Write \(m=n_{\mathrm{eff},r}\), \(h=h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and let \(Z_r=\sum_iL_i\) be the patient decomposition furnished by the pooled lemma when \(r=1\) and by the stabilized transfer lemma when \(r\ge2\). The deterministic patient envelopes in those constructions give
\[
 \|L_i\|_\infty\le
 \begin{cases}
 Cn_D^{-1},&r=1,\\
 CK_T^{-1},&i\text{ is target-pre},\\
 Cn_D^{-1},&i\text{ is a donor patient}.
 \end{cases}                                                   \tag{A.1}
\]
The same bounds hold for the observed multiplier coefficients on every regular branch. The pooled fallback has the donor bound except on the aggregate exhaustion event, whose probability is exponentially small by the risk-set argument in the pooled and stabilized lemmas.

We first compare covariance kernels. In rank one, the explicit formulas in the pooled product-limit calculation are
\[
 \Sigma_1(s,t)=\frac{s_1(s)s_1(t)}{n_D}
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\frac{\lambda_1(u)}{H_D(u)}\,du,
\]
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_1(s,t)=\widehat S_D(s-)\widehat S_D(t-)
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\frac{J_Y(u)}{Y(u)^2}\,dN(u).          \tag{A.2}
\]
On \(\{\inf_{u\le\bar\tau}Y(u)\ge n_Dh_0/2\}\), substitute \(dN=dM+Y\lambda_1du\) in (A.2). Predictable isometry, the maximal inequality, and the time-ordered empirical-risk bound give
\[
 E\sup_v\left|
 \int_0^v\frac{n_D}{Y(u)^2}\,dN(u)
 -\int_0^v\frac{\lambda_1(u)}{H_D(u)}\,du
 \right|\le Cn_D^{-1/2}.                                  \tag{A.3}
\]
The complement has probability at most \(Ce^{-cn_D}\), and the pooled survival error has squared supremum expectation at most \(Cn_D^{-1}\). Hence
\[
 E\{\rho_1^{-2}\|\widehat\Sigma_1-\Sigma_1\|_\infty\}
 \le Cn_D^{-1/2}=Ca_{1,n}.                                \tag{A.4}
\]

Now let \(r\ge2\). On the aggregate regular event, write the coordinate-free prediction map as \(F\) and its population derivative as \(DF\). Let \(\Pi\) select the positive rank-\(d\) spectral subspace and let \(A=(\Pi\Gamma\Pi)^{1/2}\) on its selected range. For a contour \(\mathscr C\) lying in the fixed spectral gap, the resolvent identity gives the explicit selected-projector perturbation
\[
 \widehat\Pi-\Pi
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\mathscr C}
 (z-\widehat\Gamma)^{-1}(\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma)
 (z-\Gamma)^{-1}\,dz.
\]
The positive-square-root derivative is the unique selected-range solution of
\[
 A\,DA_\Gamma[E]+DA_\Gamma[E]A
 =D(\Pi\Gamma\Pi)_\Gamma[E].
\]
The contour distance and the selected eigenvalue lower bound make both displayed derivative maps uniformly Lipschitz. With \(H=A_0^*A_0\), the inverse pre-Gram perturbation is controlled by
\[
 \widehat H^{-1}-H^{-1}
 =\widehat H^{-1}(H-\widehat H)H^{-1},
\]
and the two pre-Gram inverses are uniformly bounded by the fixed positive Gram thresholds. These three identities, differentiated once where necessary, imply
\[
 \|D\widehat F-DF\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C\{K_T^{-1/2}+n_D^{-1/2}+\eta_D(K_D)\}              \tag{A.5}
\]
in mean, after truncation at the fixed spectral and pre-Gram thresholds. For a stabilized cell of size \(k\), write \(H_k=S^0G\), and define the naturally normalized oracle and empirical cell covariance kernels by
\[
 V_k(s,t)=S^0(s)S^0(t)\int_0^{s\wedge t}
 \frac{\lambda^0(u)}{H_k(u)}\,du,
\]
\[
 \widehat V_k(s,t)=k\widehat S_k^\dagger(s-)
 \widehat S_k^\dagger(t-)
 \int_0^{s\wedge t}\{Y_k^\dagger(u)\}^{-2}\,dN_k(u).
\]
Substitution of \(dN_k=dM_k+Y_k\lambda^0du\), clipping at \(kh_0/8\), the Lipschitz identity for the inverse risk, and predictable isometry give
\[
 E\sup_{s,t}\left|\widehat V_k(s,t)-V_k(s,t)\right|
 \le Ck^{-1/2},                                           \tag{A.6}
\]
The difference is the martingale term with integrand \(k/Y_k^{\dagger 2}\), the inverse-risk replacement term, and the two survival-factor replacements; clipping bounds every integrand on every dataset, while the stabilized cell lemma bounds the last two replacements. The deterministic stabilized bias contributes \(C\eta_D(K_D)\), while target and aggregate fallback events contribute \(Ce^{-c_0K_T/2}+Ce^{-c_0n_D/2}\). Composing (A.5)--(A.6), using (A.1), and summing the independent target and donor covariance blocks yields
\[
 E\{\rho_r^{-2}\|\widehat\Sigma_r-\Sigma_r\|_\infty\}
 \le Ca_{r,n}.                                            \tag{A.7}
\]
Markov's inequality applied to (A.4) or (A.7), together with the exponentially small aggregate fallback event, gives a measurable event \(\mathcal E_{r,n}^{\mathrm{cov}}\) such that
\[
 \sup_PP\{(\mathcal E_{r,n}^{\mathrm{cov}})^c\}\le Ca_{r,n}^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Sigma_r-\Sigma_r\|_\infty
 \le C\rho_r^2a_{r,n}^{1/2}                              \tag{A.8}
\]
on that event.

It remains to control time increments of the realized derivative. For an interval \(J=(g,g']\) with grid endpoints, let \(N_T(J)\) and \(N_D(J)\) count observed failures in the target-pre and pooled donor blocks, respectively; omit \(N_T\) at rank one. Hazard smoothness implies
\[
 EN_T(J)\le LK_T|J|,
 \qquad EN_D(J)\le Ln_D|J|.                               \tag{A.9}
\]
Bernstein's exponential-moment argument for sums of independent Bernoulli variables, followed by a union bound over at most \(|\mathcal G|^2\) intervals, gives an event \(\mathcal E_{r,n}^{\mathrm{inc}}\) on which
\[
 N_T(J)\le C K_T(|J|+h),
 \qquad N_D(J)\le C n_D(|J|+h)                            \tag{A.10}
\]
for every grid interval, and
\[
 \sup_PP\{(\mathcal E_{r,n}^{\mathrm{inc}})^c\}
 \le C|\mathcal G|^2e^{-cmh}.                             \tag{A.11}
\]
Here \(mh\to\infty\) polynomially because \(h\asymp\rho_r^{1/q_\beta}\), \(q_\beta>3/2\), and \(\rho_r\asymp m^{-1/2}\). Thus (A.11) is bounded by \(Ca_{r,n}^{1/2}\) on every sufficiently large tail.

The derivative increment between \(g\) and \(g'\) is the sum of a Lipschitz coefficient change and the patient failures in \(J\). Equations (A.1) and (A.10), Gaussian isometry, and \(K_T^{-1}+n_D^{-1}\le\rho_r^2\) give, for distinct grid points,
\[
 \widehat d_r(g,g')^2
 \le C\rho_r^2|g-g'|^2
 +C\{K_T^{-2}N_T(J)+n_D^{-2}N_D(J)\}
 \le C\rho_r^2|g-g'|.                                    \tag{A.12}
\]
The last step uses \(|g-g'|\ge h\). Taking expectations in the same calculation gives the oracle bound \(d_r(g,g')^2\le C\rho_r^2|g-g'|\). Intersecting the two events in (A.8) and (A.11) proves the covariance and semimetric assertions.

Finally, for fixed \(g,g'\), the independent centered increment \(Z_r(g)-Z_r(g')\) has variance at most \(C\rho_r^2|g-g'|\) and summand envelope at most \(C\rho_r m^{-1/2}\) by (A.1) and \(\rho_r\asymp m^{-1/2}\). The exponential Markov proof of Bernstein's inequality therefore gives
\[
 P\{|Z_r(g)-Z_r(g')|>x\}
 \le2\exp\left[-c\min\left\{
 \frac{x^2}{\rho_r^2|g-g'|},
 \frac{x\sqrt m}{\rho_r}\right\}\right].               \tag{A.13}
\]
Set
\[
 x=C\rho_r\left[\{u\log(e p_{\mathcal G})\}^{1/2}
 +m^{-1/2}\log(e p_{\mathcal G})\right].
\]
For \(|g-g'|\le u\), (A.13) is at most \(2p_{\mathcal G}^{-6}\) after enlarging \(C\). A union bound over at most \(p_{\mathcal G}^2\) signed pairs proves the displayed modulus probability. No variance was inverted at any step.

\emph{Coarse-net and conditional Gaussian comparison.}
We first couple the oracle process to its Gaussian counterpart. Let \(k=k_{r,n}\), and choose a deterministic subset \(\mathcal T_n\subset\mathcal G\) of at most \(k+1\) knots whose physical-time mesh is at most \(C/k\). Evaluate both signs of every normalized patient vector on \(\mathcal T_n\); the ambient dimension is at most \(p_{\mathrm c,r,n}\). From (A.1), separately summing the target and donor blocks,
\[
 \sum_iE\|L_i/\rho_r\|_{2,\mathcal T_n}^3
 \le Cp_{\mathrm c,r,n}^{3/2}m^{-1/2}.                    \tag{B.2}
\]
We invoke Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014), Theorem~4.2, directly.  In the finite-dimensional form used here, if \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent centered vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\) are independent centered Gaussian vectors with \(E(Y_iY_i^\top)=E(X_iX_i^\top)\), and \(a>0\), then, with
\[
 B_0=pa^{-3}\sum_{i=1}^N E\|X_i\|_2^3,
\]
there is a coupling satisfying
\[
 P\left\{\left\|\sum_iX_i-\sum_iY_i\right\|_2>3a\right\}
 \le C B_0\left\{1+\frac{|\log(1/B_0)|}{p}\right\}.
\]
No covariance nonsingularity condition is imposed.  Apply this theorem to the signed coarse-net patient vectors with \(a=U_{r,n}^{1/4}\).  By (B.2), its dimension-adjusted quantity satisfies
\[
 B_0\le C p_{\mathrm c,r,n}^{5/2}m^{-1/2}a^{-3}
 \le U_{r,n}^{1/4}.                                      \tag{B.3}
\]
Thus a centered Gaussian vector \(G_r\) with the covariance of \(Z_r\) can be coupled on \(\mathcal T_n\) so that the Euclidean error is at most \(C\zeta_{r,n}\) except on an event of probability at most \(C\zeta_{r,n}\). This step permits a singular covariance matrix.

The interval-count, semimetric, and Bernstein bounds (A.9)--(A.13) transfer this coupling to the canonical grid. Indeed, with \(u=C/k\), its Bernstein bound gives
\[
 \max_{\substack{g,g'\in\mathcal G\\|g-g'|\le u}}
 |Z_r(g)-Z_r(g')|\le C\rho_r\zeta_{r,n}                  \tag{B.4}
\]
outside an event of probability at most \(p_{\mathcal G}^{-4}\). For the Gaussian process, the same semimetric bound makes each such increment Gaussian with variance at most \(C\rho_r^2u\); a union bound over at most \(p_{\mathcal G}^2\) pairs gives the analogue of (B.4) with failure at most \(p_{\mathcal G}^{-4}\). The relations \(k\asymp m^{1/9}\), \(\rho_r\asymp m^{-1/2}\), and \(|\mathcal G|\le C\rho_r^{-1/q_\beta}\) show that both modulus allowances and failures are dominated by \(C\zeta_{r,n}\). Consequently, for every real \(x\),
\[
 P\{\|G_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le x\}
 \le P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le x+C\rho_r\zeta_{r,n}\}+C\zeta_{r,n}.              \tag{B.5}
\]

We next compare \(G_r\) with the conditional Gaussian process \(\widehat G_r\) having covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_r\). Put \(a_n=a_{r,n}\) and \(v_n=a_n^{1/2}\). On the event \(\mathcal E_{r,n}=\mathcal E_{r,n}^{\mathrm{cov}}\cap\mathcal E_{r,n}^{\mathrm{inc}}\) constructed in (A.8)--(A.11),
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_r-\Sigma_r\|_\infty
 \le C\rho_r^2v_n,\qquad
 P(\mathcal E_{r,n}^c)\le Cv_n.                           \tag{B.6}
\]
Choose an auxiliary subset of the canonical grid with mesh at most \(u_n=v_n^{1/3}\) and cardinality \(K_n\le Cv_n^{-1/3}\). On that subset the two covariance matrices differ in trace norm by at most \(CK_n^2\rho_r^2v_n\). Powers and St{\o}rmer (1970), Lemma~4.1, states in finite dimension that, for positive semidefinite matrices \(A\) and \(B\),
\[
 \|A^{1/2}-B^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le\|A-B\|_*.
\]
Applying this inequality and using a common standard-normal vector therefore gives a coupling satisfying
\[
 E\|G_r-\widehat G_r\|_{2,\mathrm{aux}}
 \le C\rho_rK_nv_n^{1/2}\le C\rho_r a_n^{1/12}.          \tag{B.7}
\]
The semimetric bound and a Gaussian union bound transfer (B.7) to the canonical grid with expected modulus at most
\(C\rho_r a_n^{1/12}\{1+|\log a_n|\}^{1/2}\). Markov's inequality at the larger threshold
\[
 \rho_r a_n^{1/48}\{1+|\log a_n|\}                      \tag{B.8}
\]
shows, conditionally on the data in \(\mathcal E_{r,n}\), that the difference of the two Gaussian suprema exceeds (B.8) with probability at most the normalized quantity in (B.8), for every sufficiently large tail. The complement probability \(Cv_n\) is also dominated by (B.8).

Combining (B.5)--(B.8) and the definition of \(\chi_n\) yields, on \(\mathcal E_{r,n}\), the one-sided comparison
\[
 \widehat F_r(x)
 \le F_{r,P}(x+\rho_r\chi_n)+\chi_n
 \quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R,                    \tag{B.9}
\]
where
\[
 F_{r,P}(x)=P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le x\},
 \quad
 \widehat F_r(x)=P_\xi\{\|\widehat Z_r^\xi\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le x\mid O\}.
\]
No anti-concentration or coordinate-variance division is used.

The rates are explicit. Since \(p_{\mathrm c,r,n}=O(m^{1/9})\),
\[
 U_{r,n}=O(m^{-2/9}),\qquad
 \zeta_{r,n}=O\{m^{-1/18}(1+\log m)\}.                   \tag{B.10}
\]
Also \(a_{r,n}\to0\) uniformly on every three-dimensional tail. Hence \(\chi_n\to0\) and \(\tau_n/\rho_r=\chi_n\to0\). Because \(\delta_n\) decreases only at the displayed iterated-logarithm rate, while both terms in \(\chi_n\) decrease at a positive power of the tail index up to logarithms, eventually
\[
 2\chi_n\le\delta_n/2.                                    \tag{B.11}
\]

Let \(q_n=1-\alpha+\delta_n\), and let
\(c_{r,P}(u)=\inf\{x\ge0:F_{r,P}(x)\ge u\}\). The conditional Gaussian maximum is a Borel function of a finite standard-normal vector and its observed covariance matrix. Taking the infimum over nonnegative rationals proves measurability of \(\widetilde c_r^\xi\), including singular covariance and the identically zero process. Its generalized-inverse property and (B.9) give on \(\mathcal E_{r,n}\)
\[
 \widetilde c_r^\xi+\rho_r\chi_n
 \ge c_{r,P}(q_n-\chi_n).                                 \tag{B.12}
\]
The right side is deterministic for fixed \(P\). Therefore, without any independence between \(\mathcal E_{r,n}\) and \(Z_r\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le
 \widetilde c_r^\xi+\tau_n\}
 &\ge q_n-\chi_n-P(\mathcal E_{r,n}^c)\\
 &\ge1-\alpha+\delta_n/2,
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{B.13}
\]
after absorbing the event probability into \(\chi_n\) and using (B.11).

Finally, \(q_n\le1-\alpha/2\). Conditional Markov inequality gives
\[
 \widetilde c_r^\xi\le
 \left\{\frac2\alpha E_\xi
 \|\widehat Z_r^\xi\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2\right\}^{1/2}. \tag{B.14}
\]
The pooled and stabilized moment bounds, followed by Jensen's inequality, yield
\(\sup_PE_P\widetilde c_r^\xi\le C\rho_r\). Equations (B.10)--(B.14) prove every assertion, including zero-variance time zero. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Han and Shah's Theorem~1 structural model requires a finite-dimensional survival factorization \(S^{(0)}_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p(t),v_m\rangle\) and, separately, inclusion of each treated-unit factor \(v_\star\) in the linear span of the donor factors.  The well-conditioned finite-grid pre-period matrix and latent time-period span restrictions are introduced later as Assumptions~7 and~8 for their Theorem~2, not as conditions of their Theorem~1.

source.locator: Assumptions 4 and 6 and Theorem 1 in Section 3.4.1; Assumption 7 in Section 3.4.3
source.verbatim_statement: Assumption 4 (Survival Factor Model). For all \(p\in[P]\), \(n\in[N]\) and \(t\in[0,\widetilde{\tau}]\), the potential survival function under control \(S^{(0)}_{p,n}(t)=\langle u_p(t),v_n\rangle\), where \(u_p:[0,\widetilde{\tau}]\to\mathbb R^r\) are (latent) period factors and \(v_n\in\mathbb R^r\) are (latent) unit factors for some \(r\ge1\). Assumption 6 (Linear Span Inclusion). For each treated unit \(n\in\mathcal I^{(1)}\), there exists weights \(w_{n,m}\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal I^{(0)}|}\) such that \(v_n=\sum_{m\in\mathcal I^{(0)}}w_{n,m}\cdot v_m\). Theorem 1. Given the assumptions above, we have \(S^{(0)}_{1,n}(\cdot)=\sum_{m\in\mathcal I^{(0)}}w_{n,m}S^0_{1,m}(\cdot)\). Assumption 7 (Well-conditioned Spectrum). The expectation of the control group pre-treatment matrix satisfies: \(\operatorname{cond}(\mathcal S_{0,\mathcal I^{(0)}})\le\xi'\), and \(\|\mathcal S_{0,\mathcal I^{(0)}}\|_F^2\ge\xi''N_0T_0\) for some constants \(\xi',\xi''>0\), where \(\|\cdot\|_F\) is the Frobenius norm. Assumption 8 (Latent time-period span). We assume the post-period specific factors lie in the span of pre-period specific factors, i.e., \(\forall t\in\mathcal T,u_1(t)\in\operatorname{span}(\{u_0(s):s\in\mathcal T\})\) conditional on \(\{\mathcal{LF},\mathcal D\}\).

statements.statement:
Suppose an affine survival panel satisfies
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d,
 \qquad d=r-1.
\]
Set \(u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t)=(s_p(t),b_p(t)^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\) and \(v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}=(1,z_m^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\).  Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t),v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}\rangle\), the donor loading matrix \(V_D=[v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D]\) has full row rank \(r\), and \(v_\star^{\mathrm{HS}}\in\operatorname{span}\{v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D\}\).  In particular, every \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) is a specialized subclass member of the Han--Shah Theorem~1 survival factor model with donor-span inclusion; this implication does not assert that Han and Shah impose the canonical normalization, exact centered rank, spectrum, pre-Gram, smoothness, or loading-envelope restrictions defining \(\mathfrak P_r\).
statements.justification: This algebraic certificate locates the note's canonically normalized class as a strict specialization of the published Theorem~1 structural model without attributing the note's quantitative restrictions to Han and Shah.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC states generic factorization and donor-span inclusion but does not use the centered donor normalization or exact contrast-rank parameterization proved here.
statements.consumer: It licenses upward transfer of lower bounds by subclass inclusion while blocking any converse claim that the published class inherits this note's functional-PCR upper theorem.

statements.statement:
Let \(\theta_Q(t)=S^0_{1,\star}(t)\) for \(Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).  There are constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_\star>0\), independent of \(N_0,K_T,K_D\), such that, whenever \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\),
\[
 c_\star\le
 \inf_{B:\ \inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}
 Q\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta_Q(t)\le B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
 \text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}
 \ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}
 \ \sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}E_Q\{w(B)\}
 \le1.
\]
Hence the minimax expected supremum width over the donor-visible known-rank-two class has sharp order one.  Every member of this class has normalized contrast indicator one, full-row-rank donor loadings, and target loading in the donor span; in the fixed-design experiment it is therefore inside the factorization-and-span model used by Han--Shah Theorem~1.

The weak-pre-Gram pair \(\mathbb W_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) in \(\mathrm{def:weak\mbox{-}pre\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}pair}\) satisfies
\[
 \{Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}}\}
 \subset\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D),
 \qquad
 \sigma_T=\{K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2\}^{1/2}\|\psi_\circ\|_2,
 \qquad
 H_{0,T}=K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2,
\]
so \(\sigma_T\ge|a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2>0\) while \(H_{0,T}\to0\).  Its target separation is a fixed positive constant and
\(\operatorname{TV}(Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}})=O(K_T^{-1/2})\).

For a finite pre-period grid \(\mathcal T=\{t_1,\ldots,t_{T_0}\}\), put \(a=(e^{-\lambda_\circ t_\ell})_\ell\) and \(q=(\psi_\circ(t_\ell))_\ell\).  If \(a\) and \(q\) are linearly independent, the pair's pre-period donor matrix has rank two and the ratio of its largest to smallest nonzero singular value is at least a fixed positive constant times \(K_T\), so Han--Shah Assumption~7 fails for all sufficiently large \(K_T\).  If \(q\ne0\) is collinear with \(a\), the pre-period latent-factor span is one-dimensional and Han--Shah Assumption~8 fails for all sufficiently large \(K_T\).  If \(q=0\) on the grid, Assumptions~7--8 may hold, but the grid observes none of the perturbation and Han--Shah Theorem~2 does not address the pair's nonzero continuous-time target separation between grid points.  Thus the lower bound does not contradict their Theorem~2, and the functional-PCR upper bound over \(\mathfrak P_2\) does not transfer to this larger weak-pre-Gram class.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(c_T=K_T^{-1}\), let \(\widetilde z_m\) be the unoriented donor scores in the weak-pair construction, put
\[
 \bar h=\frac12\min\{h_\circ,R_1,M_\star\}>0,
 \qquad q_\alpha=\frac12-\alpha>0,                       \tag{1}
\]
and suppress the fixed sign \(\varsigma_T\) whenever it cancels from a product.

We first verify the structural assertions for the whole class.  Every \(Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}\) has contrast indicator one and normalized scalar loadings satisfying
\[
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}^2=1.          \tag{2}
\]
Applying the algebraic part of the structural-embedding proposition with \(d=1\), the donor loading matrix with columns \((1,\zeta_{m,Q})^\top\) has full row rank two, and \((1,\zeta_{\star,Q})^\top\) lies in its column span.  The visibility lower bound makes the joint contrast factor nonzero.  Thus the total factor rank is two, and the cited scope lemma places every fixed-design member inside the factorization-and-span model used by Han--Shah Theorem~1.

We next validate the two laws in \(\mathbb W_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).  Direct summation of the centered arithmetic progression gives
\[
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde z_m=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde z_m^2=1.       \tag{3}
\]
Multiplying both the factors and loadings by \(\varsigma_T\) preserves every survival curve and enforces the prescribed sign convention.  For a donor, the pre-period curve is the witness curve with scalar coordinate \(c_T\widetilde z_m\), and the post-period curve is the witness curve with coordinate \(\widetilde z_m\).  For the target under sign \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), the corresponding coordinates are \(c_Tu\bar h\) and \(u\bar h\).  Because \(c_T\le1\), \(\max_m|\widetilde z_m|\le R_1\), and \(\bar h\le\min\{R_1,M_\star\}/2\), the explicit witness-compatibility assumption gives normalization at zero, values in \([s_-,1]\), monotonicity, the failure-density floor on \(\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')\), and the stated Hölder hazard bound.  The same assumption gives the factor envelope, and the loading bounds follow from the preceding inequalities.  Infinite censoring gives \(G=1\ge g_-\); consistency, independent censoring, and mutual patient independence hold by construction.  The exponential continuation is common to the two signs because the smooth zero extension of \(\psi_\circ\) vanishes at \(\bar\tau\).

Since the donor score in (3) has empirical second moment one, the invariant joint contrast singular value and pre-period Gram are
\[
 \sigma_T=\{K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2\}^{1/2}
             \|\psi_\circ\|_2,
 \qquad
 H_{0,T}=K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2.       \tag{4}
\]
Thus \(\sigma_T\ge |a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2>0\), while \(H_{0,T}\to0\).  Moreover, the visibility threshold in the class definition is satisfied because \(\sigma_T\ge |a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), which is twice that threshold.  Equations (3)--(4), together with the law checks above, prove
\[
 \{Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}}\}
 \subset\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D).       \tag{5}
\]

We also verify the comparison with the later Han--Shah conditions.  For a finite pre-period grid, set
\[
 a=(e^{-\lambda_\circ t_\ell})_{\ell=1}^{T_0},
 \qquad q=(\psi_\circ(t_\ell))_{\ell=1}^{T_0}.
\]
The pre-period donor matrix is
\[
 M_{0,T}=a\mathbf1^\top+c_Ta_{\circ,0}q\widetilde z^\top. \tag{6}
\]
The two right vectors in (6) are orthogonal by (3).  If \(a\) and \(q\) are linearly independent, then \(M_{0,T}\) has rank two.  Evaluating its operator norm on \(N_0^{-1/2}\mathbf1\) and using the rank-one perturbation inequality for its second singular value gives
\[
 s_1(M_{0,T})\ge\sqrt{N_0}\|a\|_2,
 \qquad
 s_2(M_{0,T})\le c_T|a_{\circ,0}|\sqrt{N_0}\|q\|_2.    \tag{7}
\]
Hence the ratio of the largest to the smallest nonzero singular value is at least a fixed positive constant times \(K_T\), and Assumption~7 fails for all sufficiently large \(K_T\).  If \(q=\kappa a\ne0\), every pre-period latent vector is proportional to
\[
 (1,\varsigma_Tc_Ta_{\circ,0}\kappa)^\top,              \tag{8}
\]
whereas the post-period vectors on the same grid are proportional to
\((1,\varsigma_Ta_{\circ,1}\kappa)^\top\).  Since \(a_{\circ,1}\ne0\), these directions differ for all sufficiently large \(K_T\), so Assumption~8 fails.  If \(q=0\), the finite grid observes none of the contrast perturbation; even if the two later assumptions happen to hold, they do not control the fixed nonzero continuous-time separation between grid points.  These exhaustive cases show that the lower pair does not contradict Han--Shah Theorem~2.

It remains to prove the minimax bound.  All observed donor cells are identical under the two signs, and the target-post cell is unobserved.  Hence the observed laws differ only through the \(K_T\) target-pre failure times.  Their causal target curves are
\[
 \theta_u(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+u\bar h a_{\circ,1}\psi_\circ(t),
 \qquad
 \Delta_\star:=\|\theta_+-\theta_-\|_\infty
 =2\bar h|a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_\infty>0.         \tag{9}
\]
On \([0,\bar\tau]\), the one-patient target-pre density is
\[
 f_u(t)=\lambda_\circ e^{-\lambda_\circ t}
        -u c_Ta_{\circ,0}\bar h\psi_\circ'(t).          \tag{10}
\]
Outside the support of \(\psi_\circ'\) the two densities agree, and after \(\bar\tau\) their continuations agree.  On that support, the witness density floor gives \(f_-\ge c_f\).  Therefore the elementary inequality \(\log x\le x-1\) and equality of the total masses imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(f_+\|f_-)
 &\le \int\frac{(f_+-f_-)^2}{f_-}\,dt\\
 &\le \frac{4c_T^2a_{\circ,0}^2\bar h^2}{c_f}
       \int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2\,dt.
 \end{aligned}                                           \tag{11}
\]
Patient independence and additivity of relative entropy over product laws now give
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}}\|Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}})
 \le \frac{C_0}{K_T}.                                    \tag{12}
\]
The revalidated Pinsker lemma yields
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}})
 \le\{C_0/(2K_T)\}^{1/2}=O(K_T^{-1/2}).                 \tag{13}
\]

Let \(B\) be any band satisfying the displayed honesty constraint, and let \(E_u\) denote simultaneous coverage of \(\theta_u\).  By honesty and total-variation transfer,
\[
 Q_-^{\mathrm{wk}}(E_-\cap E_+)
 \ge 1-2\alpha-2\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)
      -\operatorname{TV}(Q_+^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_-^{\mathrm{wk}}). \tag{14}
\]
The definition of the honesty tolerance gives \(\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\le q_\alpha/4\).  By (13), for all sufficiently large \(K_T\), the total variation is at most \(q_\alpha/2\).  Since \(1-2\alpha=2q_\alpha\), (14) is at least \(q_\alpha\).  On \(E_-\cap E_+\), the band contains both target curves at every time, and hence \(w(B)\ge\Delta_\star\).  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}E_Qw(B)
 \ge Q_-^{\mathrm{wk}}(E_-\cap E_+)\Delta_\star
 \ge q_\alpha\Delta_\star=:c_\star>0.                 \tag{15}
\]
The constant band with lower endpoint zero and upper endpoint one is continuous, has coverage one for every survival curve, and has width one.  It supplies the matching upper bound.  Thus the minimax expected supremum width has sharp order one.  The converse transfers upward from the explicit subclass, while the functional-PCR upper theorem over the smaller positive-pre-Gram class \(\mathfrak P_2\) does not transfer to \(\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}\). \(\square\)

sampling_model.design: Fixed two-period panel with one target unit observed under control only before intervention and \(N_0\) donor units observed under control in both periods.
sampling_model.units: Independent right-censored patient records within the target-pre cohort and every donor-period cohort.
sampling_model.treatment: The target receives treatment after the intervention; its missing post-control survival curve is the causal estimand, while donor exposure remains control.
sampling_model.overlap: Event and censoring survival probabilities are uniformly positive on \(\mathcal I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The primitive centered donor survival operator has exactly \(r-1\) bounded nonzero singular directions. Cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves feed the corresponding covariance-normalized functional-PCR map, and patient-level counting-process multipliers jointly re-estimate donor and target-pre uncertainty.

estimand_functional:
The observed-data functional is the random-quantile pair \((\widehat\theta_r,\widehat B_r)\), with \(c_r^\xi=\widetilde c_r^\xi+\tau_{r,n}\). Its minimax guarantees are
\[
 W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}
\]
and, for every fixed \(r\ge2\),
\[
 c\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\le W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 \le C\{\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)+\eta_D(K_D)\}.
\]
The higher-rank width is of order \(\rho_r\) only on subregimes with \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r)\). Moreover,
\[
 \inf_{B:\ \inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}Q\{\theta_Q\in B\}\ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}
 \sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}E_Qw(B)\asymp1.
\]

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 uses survival-factor representation and treated-unit donor-span inclusion; Theorem 2 additionally uses Assumption 7 finite-grid pre-matrix conditioning and Assumption 8 latent time-period span, with the weak pair related by the theorem's exhaustive grid case split.
Lemma 1 combines in-sample weight uncertainty and out-of-sample prediction uncertainty into a scalar conditional prediction interval.
Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 identify the minimum-norm PCR coefficient and control fixed-design out-of-sample prediction under row-space inclusion.
The main bootstrap theorem validates time-simultaneous martingale-multiplier bands for cumulative-hazard and survival functionals.
The paper derives synthetic-control limit laws whose relevant randomness changes with unit-level and time-level confounding.
Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 connect honest rank adaptation to minimax composite testing and oracle confidence sets in matrix completion.

tldr: The project studies the entire post-control survival trajectory for a treated unit in the exact-factor Synthetic Survival Control model. Exact total rank is imposed primitively through a centered donor survival operator with exactly \(r-1\) nonzero directions and bounded contrast spectrum, which makes the covariance-normalized factor coordinates and functional PCR well defined. At exact rank one there is no target loading to estimate, so the optimal per-triple honest band has donor-patient width \((N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\); at every fixed rank at least two, target-pre loading uncertainty survives and the sharp width is \(K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\). A censoring-aware functional-PCR band attains this frontier under a deterministic coverage-error schedule that vanishes on every three-dimensional tail, while explicit normalization-preserving survival-law pairs give the matching converse without relative-growth restrictions.

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah establish identification and finite-grid consistency for Synthetic Survival Control but do not provide uniformly honest continuous-time bands, patient-level propagation through PCR, or a minimax converse; their PETAL interval resamples donors only.
project_justification.niche: Normalization \(S(0)=1\) creates a rank-specific information geometry absent from scalar synthetic-control inference: a primitive zero-rank donor contrast operator has no heterogeneous target loading, whereas every positive fixed contrast rank can carry a target-pre channel.
project_justification.fill: The project derives canonical coordinates from an exact-rank, bounded-spectrum donor operator, defines minimax width over bands constrained at each evaluated sample triple, obtains an arbitrary-relative-growth functional expansion and attaining multiplier band, and supplies matching lower bounds including an explicit rank-two target-loading pair.

related_work: HanShah2025SSC supplies the causal survival-panel setup, exact factor restriction, Kaplan--Meier first stages, and PCR consistency that motivate the target, but it does not analyze per-triple uniform coverage or minimax expected width. AgarwalShahShen2025PCR supplies the minimum-norm and row-space PCR map and its strong-factor geometry; the present class makes that geometry primitive through exact centered-operator rank and bounded nonzero spectrum. DoblerPaulyScheike2019 supplies the patient counting-process multiplier construction for time-simultaneous survival inference. CattaneoFengTitiunik2021 supplies the conceptual separation between pre-fit and post-prediction uncertainty for scalar synthetic controls, while the explicit rank-two survival pair here isolates the target-loading channel and calculates its likelihood divergence. ImbensViviano2026 shows in a different random-factor model that valid synthetic-control inference depends on which stochastic channel remains after conditioning. GoldsmithGrevenCrainiceanu2013 accounts for decomposition uncertainty in functional principal-component bands but has neither censoring nor a causal missing curve. CarpentierKloppLofflerNickl2018 informs the open rank-adaptation question through its testing reduction. CurthPoonNoriGonzalez2024 and AtheyBayatiDoudchenkoImbensKhosravi2021 motivate, but are not theorem-level targets of, the separate approximate-rank extension.
technical_internal_limitation: The lower frontier is minimax over an exact-rank class. It does not claim that every individual rank-at-least-two law has a nonzero target-pre variance component; a particular law with a vanishing post contrast can be easier. Exact rank is also not an approximation-bias guarantee, so approximate-rank robustness remains a distinct proposal angle.
honest_scope: The closed claims concern known fixed total rank defined by a primitive centered donor operator, exactly \(r-1\) nonzero contrast directions with uniform lower and upper spectrum bounds, independent right censoring, a fixed follow-up horizon, smooth hazards, and patient sampling in the target-pre and donor cells. Honesty is imposed at every evaluated sample triple with a fixed deterministic coverage-error allowance that vanishes uniformly on three-dimensional tails. The exact rank-one reduction recovers the classical pooled donor-post survival band. Unknown-rank adaptation remains an open-ended composite-testing question, and covariate-dependent censoring is reserved for a separate efficiency problem.
